newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse seen ending 1996 quietly.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse seen ending 1996 quietly.

text.p: The Brussels bourse was pulled to a lower close Tuesday, mainly due to a major sell-off in shares of steel cord maker Bekaert, which issued a 1996 profit warning. Dealers said the market was likely to see a slow-down in bourse activity until the new year.
Dealers said the bourse was also slightly affected by the lower Wall Street opening and the negative impact of higher than expected U.S. housing prices.
The Bel-20 share index ended down 0.60 percent or 11.16 points at 1,849.03 in moderate volume worth 2.6 billion francs of Belgian shares.
"The market was resisting well compared to other European markets, but Bekaert pulled it down," said one dealer.
Steel wire and cord maker Bekaert closed down 13.43 percent at 19,825 francs after losing over 16 percent earlier in the day.
Investors reacted strongly to Bekaert's announcement that it expected a provision for a 1.6 billion francs restructuring programme to take 1996 current profits near to breakeven.
"I'm not surprised by what happend this morning, but I was surprised by the profit warning," said analyst Peter De Neve at Bank Degroof.
Elsewhere on the bourse trade was quiet but cement maker CBR gained 0.74 percent to 2,710 francs.
"CBR is holding strong with many dealers giving recommendation to buy," said a dealer.
She added that "the impression in the market was that investors are staying put on their positions this year, waiting for 1997 to find new investment".
The bourse's Bel-20 index was seen trading between 1,820 and 1,870 before the new year, as many investors were already preparing for their Christmas holidays.
